title: The Content Studio
sub: The production system behind every B2Ne campaign: from a brief to a posted LinkedIn piece, with a check at every step.
description: The Content Studio: the production system behind B2Ne’s LinkedIn campaigns, from brief to posted piece, with videos, carousels and soundtracks built in code. Designed and run by Riya Dutta.
facts: The Haunted CRM, The Founder Bottleneck and CRM Graveyard

sections.title: A studio, not a folder of files.
sections.lead: Every post goes through the same route, and nothing is built until the words are approved.
paras: Campaigns, captions, videos and carousels all live in one place, with finished work kept apart from drafts and named by posting date, so each folder reads in posting order.

sections.title: Watch one real post go from brief to posted.
sections.intro: This is “The Night Shift”, the first post of The Founder Bottleneck. Click any stop, or press Run it and follow it through all eleven. The four stops marked RD are where I sign off.

items.d: Who it’s for, what it’s about, the format, the date and what the reader should do.
For a campaign: theme options, a scored pick, content pillars and a calendar.
Drafted to one story shape: hook, problem, turn, step, lesson.
Line by line: does every line name the exact thing? Anything under 4 out of 5 is rewritten.
The gate. Nothing is built until the words are approved.
Slides and scenes are written in code.
Videos with a synthesised soundtrack; carousels as slides plus a PDF.
Sample frames from every scene, the duration and the audio.
Dated files land in the finished folders, each with its caption beside it.
Every video with sound, every slide, every caption read aloud.

rules.d: One statement per image; one line of at most eight words per slide or scene.
No statistics, prices or figures that can’t be backed up.
Client work stays out of public posts.
Every noun has one meaning to a B2B tech founder: not “forecast” but “sales forecast”, not “list” but “CRM contact list”.
Posts show the problem and what it costs. The fix is a conversation, not a free how-to.

post.title: The Night Shift
caption: Your team logged off hours ago.
But the proposal, the pricing question and the follow-up only you can send are still open on your laptop.
So dinner waits. Then the evening goes.
The work didn't stop. It waited for you.
What's still waiting on you tonight?

sections.title: A rendering lab for what comes next.
paras: Alongside the studio sits the Motion Lab, a deterministic rendering system. A brief becomes content, content gets treatments, and motion styles, transitions, materials and effects resolve through registries into scenes.
Its catalogue tracks what’s built and what’s planned, and a rule check makes sure every render comes out the same way twice.
